newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends week 0.31 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends week 0.31 pct lower.

text.p: Casablanca stock exchange closed on Friday 0.31 percent lower, pulled down mainly by blue-chip firms such as ONA Group, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 636.41 points, down from 638.40 last Friday.
First and second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued respectively in January and May 1996, rose to 1,355 from 1,339 and to 1,175 from 1,146 dirhams.
First Moroccan private conglomerate, ONA closed at 775 dirhams, down from 778 dirhams.
Blue-chip Banque Commerciale du Maroc rose to 860 dirhams from 850 dirhams. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur closed at 597 dirhams down from 600 dirhams.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir rose to 351 dirhams from 341 dirhams.
Steel mill Sonasid fell to 540 dirhams from 550 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 21.8 from 27 million.

On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 11 million from 26.1 million dirhams. Samir and BMCE accounted for main trade during the week with respectively more than 150,000 and 128,000 shares changing hands.
